summary: Automated SCIM desync after cross-team role change causing peripheral allocation mismatch and service-account overlap
description:
Issue summary:
Automated SCIM provisioning did not reconcile a recent role transfer for an employee (SWE -> Platform) which resulted in: (1) local laptop SKU remaining assigned to the old team inventory bucket, (2) a transient duplicate service-account that overlapped permissions for a short window, and (3) the user's peripheral assignments (badge access, desk reservation) not migrating to the new office seating pool.

Impact:
- One engineer had elevated overlapping service-account keys for ~45 minutes (no evidence of misuse).
- Asset inventory shows a laptop and two monitors still under previous team asset tags causing reporting discrepancy for hardware auditors.
- Desk booking and badge access mismatch prevented the engineer from accessing the new team's office pod for one morning.

Context / Background:
- This follows a cross-team role change performed via HR (Workday) on 2026-03-09. SCIM sync jobs run hourly between Workday -> Identity Provider -> Redwood internal SCIM consumer.
- The new role triggers group membership changes (platform-team, infra-read, devbench-access).
- A concurrent, manual service-account rotation was initiated by the Security team for unrelated reasons at ~09:10 UTC on 2026-03-10.

Observed behavior:
- Workday shows new role and group assignment.
- IDP group membership updated correctly.
- Our SCIM consumer displayed the user still in the old inventory group for hardware allocation and did not remove the old service-account binding; instead it created an overlapping binding with a different naming suffix.

Expected behavior:
- SCIM consumer should: (a) atomically update group memberships, (b) migrate asset allocation records to new owning group, and (c) ensure any deprecated service-account bindings are removed or marked rotated, not duplicated.

Temporary mitigation requested:
- Patch the SCIM reconciliation to detect and remove duplicate service-account bindings for this user until a permanent fix is deployed.
- Manually reassign the laptop and monitors to the new team inventory and create an audit entry for the change.

Notes: this ticket combines access, inventory, and policy questions about acceptable remediation paths for duplicate bindings created during automated provisioning failures.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) In Workday, change an employee's department from 'swe' to 'platform' and update group mapping that triggers SCIM group changes.
2) Ensure a concurrent service-account rotation or manual key operation occurs in the same hour window.
3) Observe SCIM consumer logs for reconciliation: look for non-atomic updates, duplicate service-account names with suffixes, and asset allocation not moving groups.
4) Check hardware-inventory DB for old_team_tag remaining associated with the user's device after the SCIM run completes.
logs: 2026-03-10T09:11:02Z scim-consumer INFO reconcile: starting reconciliation run for user jdoe@redwood.com
2026-03-10T09:11:32Z scim-consumer WARN reconcile: detected existing service-account 'svc-jdoe-2023' and created 'svc-jdoe-2026-dup' instead of rotating
2026-03-10T09:12:05Z inventory-service ERROR migrate_asset: asset tag RWI-3421 still mapped to team 'swe' after expected migration
2026-03-10T09:45:00Z iam-service INFO rotation: manual rotation triggered for svc-jdoe-2023 by security@redwood.com
comments: Marissa Clarke (Reporter) 2026-03-10T10:05: We saw this manifest during a routine HR sync. User is jdoe@redwood.com. Raising to infra and security for triage.

Eliot Ramos (Assignee) 2026-03-10T11:20: Confirmed duplicate service-account detected. Holding off immediate deletion until we validate key usage. I've started a manual inventory migration and noted the change in the audit log.

Nina Alvarez (Security) 2026-03-10T12:00: Security ran a quick check against key usage and found no API access from the duplicate account. Recommend marking duplicate as disabled and schedule a clean rotation. Need approval from Policy before deletion.
Harpreet Singh (Hardware Ops) 2026-03-10T13:30: Reassigned monitors and laptop to 'platform' asset group. Updated asset tags and attached audit images to this issue (links below).

Eliot Ramos 2026-03-11T08:40: I've implemented a short-lived reconciliation hook that detects suffix-pattern duplicates and pins them for manual review instead of creating them. This reduces risk but is a temporary measure.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: race condition between SCIM consumer and a separate IAM rotation job. The consumer expects idempotent set operations but the rotation job mutates service-account names causing consumer to treat rotated account as absent and create a new one.
Checked metrics on scim-consumer: reconciliation latency spikes at the same timestamp as the rotation job; see dashboard: https://confluence.redwood.internal/dashboards/scim-reconcile-latency
Inventory projection: our migration code relies on group->team mapping in cache; cache eviction during reconcile may cause non-updated migration path. Need to instrument cache hit/miss ratio.
Related config: scim-consumer version 2.6.1 has a known non-atomic patch; PRs to address were started in infra repo (see PR #1759).
workaround: Manual audit and reassignment completed for affected user. Duplicate service-account disabled and keys archived. Short-term reconciliation hook deployed to prevent auto-creation of suffix duplicates until robust fix lands.
resolution_notes: Partial mitigation applied: hardware reassignments performed, duplicate SA disabled, short-term consumer hook deployed. Permanent fix requires making SCIM reconcile and IAM rotations mutually transactional or introducing a lock; engineering will prepare a change request. Pending Policy sign-off on automated duplicate deletion.
follow_up_actions: 1) Engineering: implement transactional reconcile or lock around user service-account operations (owner: infra-team, ETA 2026-03-24).
2) Security: finalize deletion policy for duplicate service-accounts created by automated provisioning (owner: security-policy, ETA 2026-03-18).
3) Hardware Ops: run an audit sweep for last 30 days for assets with stale team tags and reconcile (owner: hardware-ops, ETA 2026-03-20).
4) HR/People Ops: add a short pause window note in the role-change workflow to reduce concurrent manual rotations (owner: hr-ops, ETA 2026-03-21).
